correctness.rationale: For interior points clearance is the minimum unit-normal slack; its gradient has norm one on each uniquely minimizing facet region. Coarea yields the joint shell densities. One-shell positive proportional facet areas imply homothety of P_t to P by classical Minkowski surface-area uniqueness. Comparing shifted support constants constructs a common tangent inball; positive area-weighted normal equilibrium verifies maximality. Converse homothety yields constant conditional probabilities and Beta(1,d) clearance. The same normal equilibrium, together with affine independence of untested lifted normals, proves sparse tests. Numerical polygons/boxes verified independently.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a population-level geometric statistical characterization of tangential polytopes in arbitrary dimension and a surprisingly low-data certificate for quadrilaterals: matching just one named edge frequency at one positive clearance. It works without generic facet lengths, explicitly handles disappearing facets and isolates the structural reason through Minkowski uniqueness and facet equilibrium. It addresses a motivated inverse-shape problem rather than an arbitrary isolated computation.
